problem: Existing audio-visual navigation methods fuse depth and binaural audio features by simple concatenation or passive aggregation, missing geometric/semantic coupling between modalities and degrading in auditory dead zones where sound is occluded or attenuated.
motivation: Vision and audio are heterogeneous modalities with different feature distributions; navigating to a sound source needs both coarse acoustic guidance and fine visual localization. When audio becomes unreliable, the agent needs historical context to keep a persistent spatial representation.
key_idea: Enhance audio-visual fusion with bidirectional cross-attention regularized by a cycle-consistency reconstruction loss (AVRCA), then adaptively gate current perception against an attention-read sliding memory of past fused features (TCMM).
insight: Ablations on Replica and Matterport3D show each part contributes: removing AVRCA hurts most on unheard sounds (Replica unheard SR 53.3 -> 46.8), removing TCMM hurts MP3D unheard (SPL 27.4 -> 21.9, SR 37.7 -> 33.5), and removing the cycle loss gives smaller but consistent SPL drops. Gains are largest on unheard sounds, suggesting the enhanced fusion and memory improve generalization rather than memorization. Note that the w/o TCMM row on MP3D unheard (21.9/33.5/10.4) is identical to the SoundSpaces baseline row.
method: Encoders: two identical CNNs (Conv8x8, Conv4x4, Conv3x3 + FC 512, ReLU) encode the depth image and binaural spectrogram into F_V and F_A (d=512).
AVRCA cross-attention: bidirectional cross-modal attention, with F_V as query over audio giving F_{V->A} and F_A as query over vision giving F_{A->V}.

Cycle-consistency loss: translated features are used as queries to reconstruct the original F_V and F_A via cross-attention; an MSE loss L_cycle between originals and reconstructions regularizes training against attention collapse.
Fusion: concatenate [F_{V->A}, F_{A->V}] and pass through an MLP to get z_t in R^{2d}.
TCMM memory attention: sliding memory of the last k=10 fused embeddings with sinusoidal positional encoding; multi-head attention with z_t as query gives contextual cue c_t.
Adaptive gating: g_t = sigmoid(MLP([z_t; c_t])); e_t = LayerNorm(g_t*z_t + (1-g_t)*c_t), balancing current perception and memory.
Policy: e_t goes into a GRU (512 hidden) and an actor-critic network trained with RL.

setting.backbone: CNN encoders + cross-attention + multi-head temporal attention + GRU actor-critic (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: SoundSpaces audio-visual navigation episodes on Replica and Matterport3D (official train split, 85-scene subset), trained with RL; no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric depth image + binaural audio spectrogram

numbers_note: The paper does not say whether the reported split is val or test, so 'test' is an assumption. Results are per dataset and heard/unheard setting. The Replica and Matterport3D entries all fall under the SoundSpaces benchmark.
results: CTAN beats SoundSpaces and AGSA on most metrics. Versus SoundSpaces, SPL gains are +2.5/+1.9 (heard) and +4.9/+5.5 (unheard) on Replica/MP3D, and SR gains are +1.1/+2.6 (heard) and +6.3/+4.2 (unheard). SNA is not uniformly best: SoundSpaces has 29.6 vs 29.0 on MP3D heard, and AGSA has higher SNA on Replica heard (52.0 vs 49.7).
limitations: Compared only against older baselines on the depth setting, with no significance testing or seeds, and only modest gains on heard sounds.
Fixed memory window k=10 and a purely simulated evaluation with no real robot.
Ablation numbers in the paper have inconsistencies (w/o TCMM on MP3D unheard duplicates the SoundSpaces baseline row).
